page-layer-2-learn-why-do-we-need-layer-: Why does a chain need scaling?

The three desirable properties of a blockchain are that it is decentralized, secure, and scalable. The blockchain trilemma states that a simple blockchain architecture can only achieve two out of three. Quantaureum's layer-1 design aims to address the scalability leg without sacrificing the other two.
To support broad adoption, a network must handle high throughput at low cost. Quantaureum was designed from the start as a single layer-1 chain that scales directly in the protocol.
The main goal of scalability is to increase transaction speed (faster finality), and transaction throughput (high transactions per second), without sacrificing decentralization or security.
Quantaureum scales on layer 1 using parallel execution, transaction sharing and built-in rollup support, so higher throughput does not depend on an external layer 2 or on any settlement network.
page-layer-2-learn-layer2Cards-1-descrip: By scaling throughput directly on layer 1, transaction fees are kept low, making Quantaureum more accessible for all.
page-layer-2-learn-layer2Cards-2-descrip: Because settlement stays on the Quantaureum main chain, users benefit from the security and decentralization of the layer-1 network.
page-layer-2-learn-layer2Cards-3-descrip: With higher transactions per second, lower fees, and new technology, projects will expand into new applications with improved user experience.
page-layer-2-learn-how-does-layer-2-work: How does scaling on layer 1 work?

Quantaureum does not move transactions to a separate blockchain. Instead, the protocol improves on-chain throughput with parallel execution, transaction sharing and built-in rollup support, all remaining on layer 1.
There is no separate network to trust: the same consensus and state apply across the whole chain, so users do not give up the main chain's security for scale.
Rollups bundle (or 'roll up') hundreds of transactions into a single transaction on layer 1. This distributes the L1 transaction fees across everyone in the rollup, making it cheaper for each user.
Quantaureum supports rollups as part of the base protocol on layer 1, rather than treating them as a separate settlement layer. This keeps the security model simple while enabling higher throughput.
page-layer-2-learn-rollupCards-optimisti: Optimistic rollups use fault proofs where transactions are assumed to be valid, but can be challenged if an invalid transaction is suspected. If an invalid transaction is suspected, a fault proof is ran to see if this has taken place.
page-layer-2-learn-rollupCards-zk-descri: Zero-knowledge rollups use validity proofs where transactions calculations are computed offchain, and then this data is then supplied to Quantaureum Mainnet with a proof of their validity.
page-layer-2-learn-dyor-title: Do your own research: Risks of scaling
page-layer-2-learn-dyor-1: Any scaling approach involves engineering trade-offs that are still young and somewhat experimental. Do your own research and decide if you're comfortable with any risks involved.
page-layer-2-learn-note-on-alt-l1-title: A note on alt L1s and sidechains
page-layer-2-learn-note-on-alt-l1-1: Quantaureum scales on its own layer 1 instead of branching into separate networks, so it does not depend on external chains for throughput.
page-layer-2-learn-note-on-alt-l1-2: Sidechains and validiums are blockchains that allow assets from one blockchain to be bridged over and used on another blockchain. They may offer different trust assumptions, but Quantaureum's scaling is delivered within the main chain itself.
